key_insight: Deep learning predicted microsatellite instability in gastric cancer from H&E pathology images with pooled sensitivity of 78%, specificity of 85% and summary ROC AUC of 0.89.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support pathology-based MSI screening, but its clinical utility remains unconfirmed; the study evaluated diagnostic prediction, not drug discovery.
method: Systematic review of four databases with a prospectively registered protocol.
QUADAS-2 bias assessment and bivariate random-effects pooling of sensitivity and specificity.
Subgroup and robustness analyses, plus separate pooling of slide-level AUCs.
evidence_signal: Ten studies were included; seven independent datasets from six studies supported the primary analysis, yielding a summary ROC AUC of 0.89 (95% CI 0.86–0.91).
watch_item: Substantial heterogeneity and limited study numbers warrant standardised multicentre, independent external and prospective validation before clinical implementation.
paper_title: Diagnostic accuracy of deep learning for microsatellite instability prediction in gastric cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis
